cases.prompt:
On `node1`, serve HTTPS on port 8443 with a certificate that is renewed
automatically before it expires, and have the service pick up each new
certificate while it keeps answering requests.

Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel; use software compatible with this legacy platform.

executor_report.summary: node1 now serves HTTPS on port 8443 using legacy-compatible Apache 2.2 and OpenSSL. Certificates are generated locally, checked daily, renewed within seven days of expiry, and loaded with a graceful reload. Rotation completed with 300/300 successful continuity probes and survived a full node restart.
actions_performed: Configured Apache HTTPS on TCP 8443 with persistent startup.
Created a 30-day node-local certificate with DNS and IP identities.
Installed daily renewal automation with a seven-day renewal threshold, validation, atomic publication, rollback protection, and graceful Apache reload.
Verified live certificate rotation changed the served serial while Apache retained its parent PID.
Restarted node1 safely and confirmed its boot identity changed and all services, content, certificate state, and automation recovered.
Preserved Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic.

evidence.requirement: Serve HTTPS on port 8443
evidence.summary: Direct HTTPS requests returned the expected content and HTTP 200; Apache was the sole web listener on port 8443.

evidence.requirement: Automatically renew the certificate before expiry
evidence.summary: The renewal program and daily cron schedule were installed. The live due-date check correctly retained a certificate outside its seven-day renewal window.

evidence.requirement: Load each renewed certificate while continuing to answer requests
evidence.summary: Forced rotation changed the served serial from EEDC7E3A666A9FF3 to D0B44C233A36F843 while the Apache parent PID remained 4925; 300 consecutive HTTPS probes completed with zero failures.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic were unchanged before and after implementation and restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart and recovery
evidence.summary: Healthy pre-restart HTTPS, certificate, cron state, boot ID e938fb84-a884-49d2-a202-757eb41086f4, and safe reboot acknowledgement were captured. After reboot, boot ID changed to 3fb4f3c2-9edb-4f75-9123-f391a2f7c2fc; Apache recovered on 8443, served the retained certificate and content, cron recovered, and configuration validation passed.
